title: More descriptive names for some heuristic dissectors
description:
Change the human-readable names for some heuristic dissectors to make
them more descriptive.

I left the short names alone since those are probably used by end-user
programs/configs/etc. Some of those may possibly also benefit from
rewording.

notes.body:
Are those reflecting their real names as they are referred to in literature, or is this a "convenience" rename to ensure people will identify the relation from the name itself? Especially in the case of quic I would strongly recommend, that if the name is not set to be "QUIC Heuristic" I would keep it as it is. 

It those names are referred as such in literature, the change would be fine by me, otherwise it would require reviews by the original authors of those dissectors

> It those names are referred as such in literature, the change would be fine by me, otherwise it would require reviews by the original authors of those dissectors

Well, I'm posting it here for review, so... :smile: 

For heuristic dissectors which seemed to be for observing a protocol over another protocol, I changed the human-readable names to be of the form "X over Y" as this is a precedent set by many of the other heuristic dissectors.

There are several other heuristic dissectors that have "heuristic" added to their human-readable names, so this is the precedent I followed with protocols like QUIC where the heuristic seems to be for establishing the protocol's presence overall, and not over one of several possible carrier protocols.

I suggest you go to `Analyze > Enabled Protocols`, and change "in any protocol" (top right of the dialog) to "in heuristic protocols", and scroll down the list. You'll see for yourself the various ways that heuristics are (and aren't) differentiated from their base protocols and each other. That context will be helpful for you in the judgment of my changes.

Yes I know, I wrote a bunch of them. But in my case, because I also was responsible for the protocols from a standard point of view, and therefore I named them as such. But changing them for convenience should only be done either on the authors discretion or if there is documentation saying the given name is wrong. Not because it makes it better readable, because a lot of people rely on those names to be correct for documentation, and may not care if they look at a heuristic protocol or not.

Also, just for clarification, heuristic dissectors are not intended for observing a protocol over another. There main reason for existence comes from the fact, that the encapsulation for that field is not defined in such a way, that one can say with absolut certainty that a given protocol should be used for dissection.

An example. Let's assume you have a bunch of data coming in at port 5050 over UDP. Now some ports have well defined numbers, and therefore 80 is always used to dissect HTTP. Or you know, that your protocol will start with the first data byte on port 5050, and therefore you register your protocol on that port.

But you might also know, that your data will come over port 5050, but you will not know at which offset in the data set. Or there are a bunch of protocols on port 5050 and they are distinguished by "magic keywords" e.g. the first 4 bytes being defined specifically. In such cases you can use a heuristic dissector. The first thing such a dissector does is to decide, IF this data is for itself to dissect or not. It may do so by checking any number of parameters or functionality. Check out packet_opensafety.c's function of "findSafetyFrame" to give you a good idea how complicated such a method may get. Once it has decided to take the packet, it will tell the calling dissector to stop looking for another one and behave like any other dissector. Or it will decide, that the data is not suitable for this specific use case and give other heuristic dissectors a chance to investigate the same data.

Therefore renaming the dissectors makes only sense if the underlying protocol is either named as such, or if it is accepted by the people using those dissectors daily. In case of QUIC and tftp I would consider renaming those dissectors to actually be a big down the road, because now an additional information pops up that was not required nor intended.

> Yes I know, I wrote a bunch of them. But in my case, because I also was responsible for the protocols from a standard point of view, and therefore I named them as such.

Forgive me for not digging through the commit history to answer this question myself, but were you the person who gave two separate heuristics the same name of "IPDU-Multiplexer-Heuristic", and gave the name "Signal-PDU-Heuristic" to four other different heuristics? Do you consider these names to be human-readable and useful to distinguish between the different dissectors?

> Also, just for clarification, heuristic dissectors are not intended for observing a protocol over another. There main reason for existence comes from the fact, that the encapsulation for that field is not defined in such a way, that one can say with absolut certainty that a given protocol should be used for dissection.

Thank you for the thorough explanation of how heuristic dissectors work. I'm actually already familiar with this information. I was being brief in my comment in order to distinguish the "X over Y" changes from the "X Heuristic" changes, but in doing so I cost some clarity. I apologize that my over-simplification detracted from my explanation of my changes.

> Therefore renaming the dissectors makes only sense if the underlying protocol is either named as such, or if it is accepted by the people using those dissectors daily.

I submitted this patch because the human-readable names of some particular heuristic dissectors is non-intuitive and unhelpful, and I wanted to remedy that. I made some similar changes (such as QUIC) because I felt like they fit under the same umbrella. If you don't want **any** changes made to the human-readable names of the heuristic dissectors, then you could simply have said so and rejected this merge request. If there are individual changes (like QUIC) you dislike, you could comment on those changes directly in the patch, and I could submit a revised patch which would not have those particular changes.

Let me emphasize again that I'm talking about the *human readable* names of the heuristic dissectors. I'm *not* changing the short names that are used on the wireshark/tshark command lines, and as the first column of the Enabled Protocols dialog, specifically because I know that "people using those dissectors daily" depend on those short names.

In fact, people who use those heuristics every day already know what the heuristics do, and have no need to read the human-readable names. In contrast, people who are still getting used to Wireshark need descriptions to be descriptive. *That* is what I was trying to achieve.

Lacking further detail about specific changes you dislike, I've inferred the worst offenders based on your comments and reverted them in 6fb0f0c0. If you have *specific* changes you'd like to see, please mention them and I will further remedy this MR.
